datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_2.png
datas.text: Nyaa? Oh hi there, new player. My name is Ichihime. Never played Mahjong before? Oh well. Let me teach you then!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text: Mahjong consists of 34 different tiles. For each tile, there are 4 of them, so there are a total of 136 tiles. They belong to 5 groups: Man, Pin, Sou, Wind and Dragon.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text:
The objective of Mahjong is to win, of course. So how do we win a game?
In a game, each player usually has 13 tiles in hand. In every turn, you will draw a tile, so the number of tiles becomes 14. Then, you shall discard one from your hand. As you keep drawing and discarding, your hand will also change.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text: Before explaining how to win, we must first understand three terms: Sequences, Triplets and Pairs. First, we have Pairs. Pairs are made of 2 identical tiles.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text:
Triplets are made of 3 identical tiles.
And Sequences are made of 3 consecutive tiles of the same group. Look!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text: Usually, when your hand consists of 4 Sequences or Triplets + 1 Pair, you are ready to win, master! Of course, in Riichi Mahjong, you must satisfy other conditions to declare a win. We will cover them later!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text:
Of course, your hand often consists of 13 tiles only, so you need one more to win.
When you just need one more tile to win, this hand is called Tenpai (Ready Hand).
Tenpai is a necessary step before winning, so make sure you pay attention to it.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_2.png
datas.text: Make sure your hand becomes 4 Sequences or Triplets + 1 Pair nyaa!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_4.png
datas.text: Correct-nya!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text:
You can't win like this-nyaa.
Remember, your hand must be 4 Sequences or Triplets + 1 Pair.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text:
You can't win like this-nyaa.
Remember, your hand must be 4 Sequences or Triplets + 1 Pair.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_2.png
datas.text: Try another one-nya!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text:
Wrong answer-nyaa…
Remember, your hand must be 4 Sequences or Triplets + 1 Pair.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_4.png
datas.text: Correct-nya!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text:
Wrong answer-nyaa…
Remember, your hand must be 4 Sequences or Triplets + 1 Pair.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text:
Now that we have learned the tiles and some Yaku, let's check out the game interface.
Master, please look at the screen above. I shall explain to you one by one-nyaa!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text:
The “East 1” in the center means you are now at the first game of the East Wind Round. East is your current Round Wind.
X67 means the number of tiles remaining. If this number becomes 0, the current game will end.
25000 is your current points available. Think of it like your “tokens”.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text:
Each player discards their unwanted tiles in front of their hands.
You can call on the discarded tiles for Chii, Pon, and Kan.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text:
Chii is the call to complete a Sequence.
You have the option to call Chii, if the last player (the player on your left side) discarded a tile that can form a Sequence with 2 tiles in your hand. Upon calling Chii, you shall open the Sequence formed on your side, then discard a tile from your hand.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text: Here, the 7-Pin discarded by the last player can be used to form a Sequence of “678-Pin” with the 6-Pin and 8-Pin in your hand if you call Chii.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text:
Pon is the call to complete a Triplet.
You have the option to call Pon, if any player discards a tile that can form a Triplet with 2 tiles in your hand. Upon calling Pon, you shall open the Triplet formed on your side, then discard a tile from your hand.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text: This is the call to complete a Quad. Kan can be called on discarded tiles from any player. You can also make a Kan call when you have four identical tiles in your hand, or has a previously melded Triplet and then draw the fourth tile.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_2.png
datas.text: If you answer the question correctly, you can have my snack-nya!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_4.png
datas.text:
Correct! Which snack do you want to have first?
I'm not a snack-nya!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text:
Not quite right…
 Chii call is to complete a Sequence.
And a Sequence consist of three consecutive tiles of the same tile group.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text:
Not quite right…
 Chii call is to complete a Sequence.
And a Sequence consist of three consecutive tiles of the same tile group.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_2.png
datas.text: Wanna have more snacks?
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text:
Wrong-nya. Think again!
Pon call is to complete a Triplet.
And a Triplet consist of three identical tiles.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text:
Wrong-nya. Think again!
Pon call is to complete a Triplet.
And a Triplet consist of three identical tiles.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_4.png
datas.text:
Correct!
No matter how many correct answers you give, I am not a snack! I'm not a cat either-nya!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text:
This game would be too easy if that's all it takes to win. You must also have “Yaku” to win a hand.
Yaku is a specific pattern of tiles. If your hand does not satisfy any Yaku, you cannot declare a win-nya! Let me show you a few easy Yaku, master.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_2.png
datas.text:
What’s Yaku? I only play by feel-nyaa.
Just joking. The simplest Yaku is Yakuhai, which refers to Triplets of White (W), Green (G), Red (R), Prevalent Wind, or Seat Wind.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text:
There's one popular Yaku named All Simples.
To complete it, your hand must not contain any Terminal or Honor(1-Man/9-Man, 1-Pin/9-Pin, 1-Sou/9-Sou, Wind Tiles, and Dragon Tiles).
My hearing is good! This one is too easy, nyaa?
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text:
Riichi is another important Yaku.
When you achieve Tenpai without calling Chii, Pon, or Kan, you may declare Riichi.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_2.png
datas.text:
Let me give you some hints on this.
Remember, Yakuhai refers to Prevalent Wind, Seat Wind, and Dragon Tiles (White, Green, Red).
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_4.png
datas.text: Correct-nya!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text:
Wrong-nya.
Pay attention to the indicator in the middle.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text:
Wrong-nya.
Pay attention to the indicator in the middle.
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.text: For All Simples, you must not have any Terminal or Honor (1-Man/9-Man, 1-Pin/9-Pin, 1-Sou/9-Sou, Wind Tiles, and Dragon Tiles)!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_4.png
datas.text: Correct-nya!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text: All Simples must not contain any Terminal or Honor (1-Man/9-Man, 1-Pin/9-Pin, 1-Sou/9-Sou, Wind Tiles, and Dragon Tiles)!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_3.png
datas.text: All Simples must not contain any Terminal Tiles (1-Man/9-Man, 1-Pin/9-Pin, 1-Sou/9-Sou, Wind Tiles, and Dragon Tiles)!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_1.png
datas.text: That's enough for the basic rules, master! Remember, we have learned the tile groups (Man, Sou, Pin, Wind, and Dragon), 3 simple Yaku (Yakuhai, All Simples, and Riichi), and the equation of winning - 4 Sequences or Triplets + 1 Pair!
datas.name: Ichihime

datas.head: extendRes/guide/l_2.png
datas.text:
You can practice your skills with AI by creating a private game room, or if you are interested in more advanced rules you can find them by tapping the “?” icon on the top right corner!
I'm going to sleep-nyaa!
datas.name: Ichihime
